answer_1.quote: The goal of rationalization is to extract a small subset of the input (i.e., rationale) to support and explain the prediction results when yielding them.
answer_1.outputs: Generated rationales (subsequences of input text) that explain model predictions

answer_2.quote: we report the token precision, recall and F1-score to evaluate the quality of selected rationales.

answer_3.quote: considering the success of Large Language Models (LLMs), we additionally add for human evaluation (the prompt for ChatGPT is shown in Appendix C.4).

answer_4.quote: we sample 100 examples and ask three annotators who are both good at computer science and law to evaluate rationales in the charge prediction.
answer_4.guideline: we employ three metrics with an interval from 1 (lowest) to 5 to evaluate rationales, including usefulness (U), completeness (C), and fluency (F).
